title: USA Health - Automated prior authorization platform
content: USA Health, a healthcare provider organization serving more than 250,000 patients annually, struggled with manual prior authorization workflows that caused scheduling errors, care delays, and a high rate of insurance claim denials. To streamline operations, the organization implemented Experian Health's automated Authorizations platform. The deployed technology leverages artificial intelligence combined with a dynamic payer rules knowledgebase to automate the end-to-end authorization process. The AI automatically identifies whether a prior authorization is required, guides staff to the appropriate payer portal, and automates 100% of the back-end submission and tracking. Once approved, it automatically posts the authorization status directly into USA Health's Electronic Health Record (EHR) system. The software also compares authorized procedures against performed procedures to flag variances and prevent downstream billing denials. Following a phased implementation, USA Health published highly successful outcomes, including increasing daily authorizations by 100% and cutting manual administrative workloads by 50%. The automation allowed the system to expand its workflows to six distinct service lines without needing to increase administrative staff, ultimately preventing costly claim denials and ensuring patients receive timely care.

title: The Permanente Medical Group - Ambient AI scribes
content: The Permanente Medical Group (TPMG), one of the largest medical groups in the United States, faced a severe clinician burnout crisis due to the heavy administrative burden of clinical documentation. To resolve this, TPMG rolled out ambient augmented intelligence (AI) scribes designed to automate note-taking and reduce physician paperwork. The deployed technology operates by passively listening to doctor-patient conversations during clinical visits, using natural language processing and generative artificial intelligence models to capture context and synthesize the clinical details into structured, draft clinical notes. Once the system generates these drafts, physicians quickly review, edit, and sign them directly within the electronic health record system. TPMG published a follow-up analysis of this deployment in NEJM Catalyst, assessing its massive scale after one year of use. Across more than 2.5 million patient encounters, the ambient AI scribes successfully saved TPMG physicians an estimated 15,791 hours of documentation time, translating to 1,794 eight-hour workdays. Beyond time efficiency, the study highlighted substantial qualitative improvements: 82% of the participating physicians reported improved overall work satisfaction, and 84% observed a positive impact on patient-physician communication.

title: El Rio Health - AI-powered patient appointment reminders and scheduling
content: El Rio Health, a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) in Tucson, Arizona, faced high patient no-show rates and tight operating margins. Its outreach staff spent up to 20 hours per week making manual phone calls, which often went unanswered. To address this, the organization implemented an AI-powered automated appointment reminder and scheduling outreach system. The system integrates directly with El Rio's electronic health record database to extract real-time scheduling data. Using predictive analytics, the AI identifies high-risk appointments prone to no-shows and initiates personalized, bidirectional communication via SMS text and voice messages. This allows patients to confirm, cancel, or reschedule appointments instantly in two-way conversations. Within 9 months of deployment, the healthcare organization published substantial operational and financial gains. El Rio Health reduced its patient no-show rates by 32% and increased its monthly revenue by approximately $100,000. Additionally, the automation of patient outreach decreased the administrative workload of staff members by 40%, allowing them to focus more on direct clinical operations.

title: Auburn Community Hospital - Computer-assisted medical coding platform
content: Auburn Community Hospital, a 99-bed independent rural hospital in New York, faced significant revenue cycle management challenges, including slow manual coding workflows and a high volume of accounts stuck in discharged-not-final-billed status. Seeking to streamline operations and scale coding capacity without adding staff, they partnered with AGS Health to implement a computer-assisted coding solution. The hospital deployed a system built on natural language processing and machine learning algorithms. This technology automatically analyzed patient clinical documentation-including progress notes, discharge summaries, and operative reports-to extract clinical intent and suggest appropriate ICD-10 medical codes. Human coders then reviewed and validated these AI-generated suggestions, enabling a hybrid human-in-the-loop workflow. Following the implementation, the hospital achieved a 50% decrease in discharged-not-final-billed cases and over a 40% improvement in coder productivity. Additionally, they recorded a 4.6% increase in their case mix index. Operationally, these changes translated to an annual revenue boost of $1.03 million, yielding a greater than tenfold return on investment for the organization.
